issues.legal_issue: A notice warning of a contemplated enforcement action and allowing time to remedy the default can satisfy natural justice without a separate show-cause notice.
material_facts: The borrower defaulted on repayment of a loan, and earlier reminders did not mention the contemplated enforcement action.
The corporation later gave notice requiring payment by a fixed date and warning that it would take possession of the factory if payment was not made.
The borrower did not pay by the stated deadline, and the corporation took possession.
issues.conclusion: The notice satisfied the requirement of natural justice, and a separate show-cause notice was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Natural justice is flexible and depends on the facts; it requires notice of the proposed adverse consequence and an opportunity to avoid it, but not any particular form of notice. The Court relied on Section 29 of the State Financial Corporations Act and S.L. Kapoor v. Jagmohan, (1980) 4 SCC 379, for the requirement of an opportunity to represent against proposed action.

predicates.corporation_enforcement_proceeding: A financial corporation seeks to enforce a borrower's default by taking action against the borrower's property.
predicates.notice_identifies_proposed_consequence: The corporation tells the borrower what adverse action it will take if the default is not remedied.
predicates.notice_sets_cure_deadline: The corporation gives the borrower a fixed time to remedy the default before taking that action.

issues.definition: When a corporation enforcement proceeding involves notice identifying the proposed consequence and setting a cure deadline, a separate show-cause notice is not required.

issues.legal_issue: A corporation's failure to consider a borrower's representation does not require its enforcement action to be set aside where a post-decisional hearing is provided and the borrower's repayment offer is unreasonable.
material_facts: The borrower submitted a representation seeking more time to repay and proposing to clear the dues from future profits.
The corporation did not show that it had considered or responded to the representation before taking possession.
The Supreme Court gave the borrower an opportunity to make a further offer after the initial hearing.

The borrower offered a small immediate payment and proposed to repay the balance from profits after regaining possession; the Court found the offer unreasonable in light of the substantial outstanding dues and uncertainty that the business would become profitable.
issues.conclusion: Although the corporation should have acted fairly by considering and responding to the representation, the Court's post-decisional hearing and the unreasonable offer did not justify setting aside the enforcement action; the appeal was allowed, and further action permitted by law remained open to the corporation.
issues.legal_principle: A public body should act fairly and communicate its response to a representation before taking drastic action. In some cases, a post-decisional hearing may meet the requirements of natural justice. The Court considered the corporation's powers under Section 29 of the State Financial Corporations Act and the general principles of natural justice discussed in S.L. Kapoor v. Jagmohan, (1980) 4 SCC 379.

rule.if: corporation_enforcement_proceeding and borrower_submitted_representation and corporation_did_not_consider_representation and reviewing_court_provided_post_decisional_hearing and repayment_offer_unreasonable

predicates.corporation_enforcement_proceeding: A financial corporation seeks to enforce a borrower's default by taking action against the borrower's property.
predicates.borrower_submitted_representation: The borrower asks the corporation to reconsider or defer the proposed action and explains how the default may be addressed.
predicates.corporation_did_not_consider_representat: The corporation takes the proposed action without considering or responding to the borrower's representation.
predicates.reviewing_court_provided_post_decisional: A reviewing court gives the borrower an opportunity to make a further submission after the corporation has acted.
predicates.repayment_offer_unreasonable: The borrower's proposed repayment is inadequate or depends on uncertain future circumstances when compared with the outstanding debt.

issues.definition: In a corporation enforcement proceeding, if a representation was not considered but a reviewing court provides a post-decisional hearing and the repayment offer is unreasonable, the enforcement action is not set aside.
